methods.label: Large Language Models (general-purpose LLMs)
methods.description: Use of general-purpose large language models (GPT-4o/5, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek, Llama) for clinical text extraction, summarization, classification, and bioinformatics tasks. Among the fastest-growing terms in the preprint corpus.
methods.rw_feasibility_reason: high: rich free-text EHR notes + survey text; LLM APIs/local models runnable in Workbench Jupyter, though PHI egress rules constrain external API calls.

methods.label: Agentic AI / autonomous LLM agents
methods.description: Multi-step autonomous AI agents that plan, call tools, and reason over data and notebooks (e.g., single-cell analysis agents, RNA-seq pipelines). Frontier and explosively growing.
methods.rw_feasibility_reason: med: agents can orchestrate BigQuery/Jupyter analyses, but tool-calling frameworks and external model access are constrained inside the secured environment.

methods.label: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
methods.description: Grounding LLM outputs in retrieved documents/knowledge bases to reduce hallucination, for literature assistants, knowledge query, and evidence-grounded reasoning.
methods.rw_feasibility_reason: high: data dictionaries, OMOP vocab, and protocol docs make strong retrieval corpora; runnable with local embeddings in-environment.

methods.label: Chain-of-thought / reasoning prompting
methods.description: Eliciting step-by-step reasoning from LLMs (chain-of-thought, reasoning models) for clinical Q&A, diagnostic reasoning, and structured extraction.
methods.rw_feasibility_reason: med: applicable to EHR-note reasoning, but depends on access to reasoning-capable models within the Workbench compute boundary.

methods.label: Foundation models (general / pretrained)
methods.description: Large pretrained, transferable models adapted across tasks via fine-tuning. Broad term spanning modalities; a dominant emerging frame in the literature.
methods.rw_feasibility_reason: high: EHR/OMOP sequences and genotypes support pretraining/fine-tuning; Hail/Spark + GPU notebooks available.

methods.label: Genomic / DNA foundation models
methods.description: Foundation models pretrained on DNA/RNA sequence (DNA language models, long-range genomic prediction) for variant effect, regulatory, and function prediction.
methods.rw_feasibility_reason: high: AoU has population-scale WGS; sequence models can score variants for downstream PRS/association work.

methods.label: Single-cell / cell foundation models
methods.description: Foundation models for single-cell and spatial transcriptomics (cell-type annotation, perturbation, embeddings). Computational analysis methods even where the assay itself is out of scope.
methods.rw_feasibility_reason: low: AoU does not generate single-cell/spatial assays; relevant only if linking external reference atlases.

methods.label: Protein language models
methods.description: Sequence-based protein representation models (ESM-2, protein LMs) for variant/function prediction and interpretability.
methods.rw_feasibility_reason: low: AoU produces no protein sequence/structure data; only indirect use scoring coding variants from WGS.

methods.label: Transformer & deep-learning architectures
methods.description: Transformer/attention-based and other modern deep-learning architectures applied to biomedical sequence, tabular, and image data.
methods.rw_feasibility_reason: high: GPU notebooks support transformers on EHR sequences, genomics, and wearable time series.

methods.label: Graph neural networks & network analysis
methods.description: Graph-based learning and network/diffusion methods over biological graphs (gene regulatory networks, knowledge graphs, patient similarity graphs).
methods.rw_feasibility_reason: med: OMOP concept graphs and phenotype networks are buildable; less natural for AoU's tabular/genomic core but feasible.

methods.label: Generative AI / generative models
methods.description: Generative modeling (GANs, diffusion, generative deep models) for data harmonization, augmentation, and simulation-conditioned prediction.
methods.rw_feasibility_reason: med: useful for harmonizing multi-site EHR and augmenting rare phenotypes; AoU lacks imaging but has tabular/genomic targets.

methods.label: Synthetic data generation
methods.description: Generating synthetic patient/clinical records to enable sharing, augmentation, and method development while preserving privacy.
methods.rw_feasibility_reason: high: large real EHR/OMOP cohorts make AoU an ideal source for training/validating synthetic-data generators.

methods.label: Multimodal modeling / data integration
methods.description: Jointly modeling multiple data modalities (genomics + EHR + imaging + wearables + text) in unified or fusion architectures.
methods.rw_feasibility_reason: high: AoU uniquely co-locates WGS, EHR/OMOP, surveys, physical measures, and Fitbit for one cohort.

methods.label: Interpretable / explainable ML
methods.description: Methods for model interpretability and explanation (SHAP, attention attribution, mechanistic interpretability) to make predictions clinically actionable.
methods.rw_feasibility_reason: high: directly applicable to any clinical-risk model built on EHR/genomic features in the Workbench.

methods.label: Zero-shot / transfer learning
methods.description: Applying pretrained models to new tasks/populations without task-specific labels (zero-shot annotation, transfer across cohorts).
methods.rw_feasibility_reason: high: zero-shot/transfer is valuable for AoU's diverse, underrepresented populations where labels are scarce.

methods.label: Embeddings & representation learning
methods.description: Learning dense vector representations of genes, concepts, patients, or sequences for downstream prediction and similarity.
methods.rw_feasibility_reason: high: concept2vec/patient embeddings over OMOP and genotype representations are readily built.

methods.label: Polygenic risk scores / PRS methods
methods.description: Construction and evaluation of polygenic risk scores, including cross-ancestry and portability methods.
methods.rw_feasibility_reason: high: WGS + EHR outcomes + diverse ancestry make AoU a premier PRS portability resource.

methods.label: Mendelian randomization
methods.description: Using genetic variants as instrumental variables to infer causal effects of exposures on outcomes.
methods.rw_feasibility_reason: high: genome-wide genotypes + phenome-wide EHR outcomes support individual-level MR.

methods.label: Phenome-wide association (PheWAS) methods
methods.description: Scanning a genetic variant or score against the full phenome of EHR-derived phenotypes.
methods.rw_feasibility_reason: high: OMOP/EHR + genotypes are exactly the inputs PheWAS needs.

methods.label: Causal inference methods
methods.description: Structural causal models, causal discovery, and causal ML (including SHAP-based causal subgroup methods) for observational data.
methods.rw_feasibility_reason: high: large observational EHR cohorts are the core use case for causal inference.

methods.label: Target trial emulation
methods.description: Designing observational analyses to emulate a hypothetical randomized trial, reducing common biases in EHR-based comparative effectiveness.
methods.rw_feasibility_reason: high: longitudinal EHR with medications/outcomes is the canonical substrate for trial emulation.

methods.label: Time-to-event / survival ML
methods.description: Machine-learning survival models (deep survival, competing risks) for time-to-event outcomes from longitudinal records.
methods.rw_feasibility_reason: high: longitudinal EHR with dates/outcomes supports rich survival modeling.

methods.label: Federated / privacy-preserving learning
methods.description: Training models across sites without sharing raw data, plus differential privacy and other privacy-preserving techniques.
methods.rw_feasibility_reason: med: AoU is a centralized enclave, but federated methods are relevant for linking AoU with external networks (e.g., N3C/AoU).

methods.label: Digital / wearable biomarkers
methods.description: Deriving surrogate and digital biomarkers from wearable/sensor time series (actigraphy, heart rate, sleep) and linking to health outcomes.
methods.rw_feasibility_reason: high: AoU has Fitbit minute-level data linkable to EHR and genomics.

methods.label: Digital twins / in-silico modeling
methods.description: Patient-level digital-twin and simulation models that integrate physiological signals to predict individual trajectories.
methods.rw_feasibility_reason: med: feasible for wearable+EHR physiological twins, but mechanistic twins need data AoU may not fully capture.

methods.label: Benchmarking & model evaluation
methods.description: Rigorous benchmarking, calibration, and evaluation frameworks for ML/AI methods, including well-calibrated metrics and bias/hallucination assessment.
methods.rw_feasibility_reason: high: AoU's diverse cohort is ideal for fairness/calibration benchmarking of clinical models.

methods.label: Single-cell / spatial analysis methods (computational)
methods.description: Computational analysis methods originating in single-cell/spatial omics (NMF programs, trajectory inference, niche identification) that may transfer to other high-dimensional AoU data.
methods.rw_feasibility_reason: low: AoU lacks the single-cell/spatial assays these methods target; only the dimensionality-reduction techniques transfer.
